subject: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina@pioneer.ai>, PioneerAI Procurement <procurement@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)
Attachments: capacity_matrix_pioneerai_v1.xlsx, redwood_sow_draft.pdf

Hi Lina / team,

Great talking earlier this week. Per our call, I put together an initial capacity matrix and a short SOW draft so we can align on how Dedicated capacity and burst/autoscale will be handled once we move to committed slabs. The attached matrix has a steady-state profile and three peak scenarios — please confirm whether your on-prem telemetry matches the numbers.

We want to make the contract runway explicit on two things:
- Burst headroom: how many GPUs (or equivalent vGPU slots) we reserve for short spikes vs. longer uplift windows.
- Eviction & fallback: rules for preemption, fallback to smaller model variants, and any credit/backfill you'd expect if we need to throttle.

Ask: can you share your expected peak (qps or tokens/min) for the next 6 months and a sample day of peaks? Evan, if procurement needs different attachments (pricing, SOW redlines), looping you here.

Proposed next step: 30-minute tech + ops sync early next week (Karthik and Ben will join to go through sizing). If that works, Monica will send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference | developer-first runtime for LLM inference
From: Lina Park <lina@pioneer.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@pioneer.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)

Diego — thanks for this and for the matrix. Quick answers inline: 

- Steady-state: ~120 concurrent sessions during business hours (models range 2–8k tokens/session). Typical token output ~15M tokens/day.
- Peaks: we see short spikes up to 6x (lumpy traffic from nightly model evaluations and partner demo windows) that last 5–30 minutes, and occasional platform-wide batch runs that push sustained +50% for a 2–3 hour window.
- Tolerance for throttling: we prefer graceful throttling over hard failures; credits for missed SLA windows are negotiable but we'd like clear preemption semantics.

Two asks for your ops team: 1) Can Redwood guarantee locality (us-west) for burst capacity? 2) What’s your eviction order when multiple customers are bursting?

Happy to do a tech walkthrough next week.

—Lina Park
CTO, PioneerAI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)

Team — forwarding Lina's note with their rough steady-state / spike patterns. Karthik/Ben: can you review the attached matrix and run a quick topology/sizing check focused on:

1) Recommended slab carve for steady-state vs. burst pool (we want to minimize committed spend while protecting critical SLAs).
2) Locality for burst capacity (us-west preferred) and what we can commit in contract.
3) Eviction policy recommendation and customer-facing wording (what does graceful throttling look like, and when do credits apply).

Monica will coordinate an invite for early next week; Lina/Evan prefer Tue/Wed morning PT.

Diego
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@pioneer.ai>, Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@pioneer.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)

Diego / team — reviewed the matrix and ran two quick sims (attached). High-level notes:

- Baseline slab: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (steady) + a 4 GPU shared burst slab gives ~3x short spike headroom; that maps well to Lina's 5–6x short spikes if we combine intelligent batching + KV cache priming.
- Shoulder buffer: recommend an "opportunistic" buffer of 2–3 preemptible GPUs for ambient noise and demo flares; we can attach autoscale rules to open slots for <10min windows.
- Sustained uplift (2–3 hours): suggest temporary reserve policy (time-limited, billable) rather than permanent slab increases — include an explicit ramp-up/cool-down cooldown (30–60min) to avoid oscillation.
- Locality: we can reserve capacity in us-west but need a 72-hr lead window for capacity guarantees in the contract unless customer chooses dedicated racks.

Draft contract language to propose (short): 
"Redwood will maintain a Dedicated steady-state slab as specified. Short-duration burst capacity (<=30 minutes) will draw from a reserved burst pool in the same region. For sustained bursts (>30 minutes), Redwood may transition to temporary reserved capacity subject to availability and billable uplift. Eviction follows least-recently-used preemption across opportunistic pools with priority overrides for enterprise SLA tiers."

I'll be at the sync to walk through numbers.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@pioneer.ai>, Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@pioneer.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)

Quick ops notes — we should call out explicit behaviors so procurement knows what they'll get:

- GPU types: A100/80GB class for steady-state; burst pool can include A100 (non-volatile) + 1–2 preemptible A40s for short windows.
- Eviction: preemptible nodes get reclaimed first; if forced across reserved pools, we apply a cross-customer fairness policy (priority by tier and time-in-use). We can include a conservatively estimated preemption probability for planning.
- Monitoring & alerts: include token-level throttling dashboards and a per-route SL impact view in the console.
- Credits: propose a simple credit model: 1% monthly credit per incident where latency SLOs are not met due to lack of burst capacity, capped at 5%/month.

I'll attach operational definitions into the SOW appendix.

—Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina@pioneer.ai>, PioneerAI Procurement <procurement@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PioneerAI Dedicated: capacity resilience & burst policy (contract runway)

Lina / Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are the simulation results and an updated SOW appendix that includes the eviction language, burst sizing, and the credit model Ben suggested. Summary highlights:

- Recommended contract: 8 GPU steady slab + 4 GPU burst pool (region: us-west) + 2 opportunistic preemptible GPUs for <10min flares.
- Sustained uplift handling: temporary reserved uplift (billable) with 30–60min ramp/cooldown.
- Eviction & credits: preemptible reclaimed first; cross-pool fairness; credit model (1% per incident, 5% cap/month).
- Lead time: 72 hours for guaranteed regional burst capacity unless PioneerAI purchases colocated racks (we can add a clause to accelerate with an upfront deposit).

Next steps: Monica will share calendar options for Tue/Wed morning PT to finalize numbers and confirm legal language. If procurement is ready, we can send a DocuSign packet with the SOW + the burst appendix after the sync.
